title: One query-log entry that fails the store gates stays in the local store while the rest of the batch is delivered
goal: a store file that fails the leak scan at delivery stays in the local store, undelivered, and the batch's other files are copied into the delivery; the delivery log names how many files are held back with the first problem line of each

run:
import sys,json,tempfile,pathlib as P,subprocess as s
sys.path.insert(0,"_tools");import ql_deliver as D
home=P.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp());s.run(["git","-C",str(home),"init","-q"],check=True);q=P.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp());local=q/"store"

 f=local/rel;f.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True);f.write_text(json.dumps({"id":"x","note":note})+"\n");return f

gates.question: How long may a store file stay held back from delivery, since the held-back data stays local and unreviewed?
options: No limit: it is retried at every delivery and delivered once the gates pass it; the delivery log names the count
It is retried at every delivery, and kbmon names a file held back for more than 7 days

gates.reason: the held-back count in the delivery log already shows a stall, and an age alert is a later item

notes: From the 2026-10-24 telemetry and query-log analysis: distill.log shows 72 'apply --push: refused: the store gates fail on the local store's files; nothing committed or pushed' since 10-17; the longest streak is 63 refusals in a row from run 20261021T153857Z to 20261022T221356Z, about 30 hours of delivery stalled (per day, runs refused or pushed: 10-21 46/26, 10-22 17/13, 10-23 8/72, 10-24 0/119) and 25,338 spool rows waiting now. Causes named under the refusal: 49 times 'the leak scan flags an identifier (guid)' (one entry in a 2026-10 run file), 22 times 'fetch host is not a public host' (one entry each in a 2026-09 and a 2026-10 run file). Both were later fixed by redact commits; the next unseen shape will stall delivery the same way. ql_deliver.py:655-690 bring() returns 1 for the whole batch and nothing is committed or pushed; entries that name an internal root already stay local one by one (public_copy), so the mechanism for a per-file local keep exists. Saves a 30-hour stall and the wait for a redaction fix before any lookup data reaches the repository. Also wanted, not read by the planted run: kbmon's query-log panel shows the count of held-back files, a held-back file is retried at the next delivery and delivered once the gates pass it, and an entry-level gate (entry_problems) holds back the same way. Medium confidence: the held-back data stays local and unreviewed, so the operator may want a gate on how long. The fixture's id-shaped value is built at run time so the item file carries none. Premise: both checks fail on the base: with one clean file and one holding a guid-shaped value, bring() returns 1 and the delivery is refused as a whole (nothing committed or pushed): the failing file is not held back, and the log names no held-back count.
